keyECGEvidence: AV dissociation with 2 capture beats visible
RBBB-like morphology with monophasic R in V1 and QS pattern in V6
modelResponse.mechanism: Re-entry within scarred myocardium secondary to prior anterior MI and LVEF 35%
contributingFactors: Prior anterior MI (2020, PCI to LAD)

rejectedAlternatives.why: Presence of AV dissociation and capture beats is pathognomonic for VT; axis and morphology are highly suggestive of VT over SVT.
ECG shows AV dissociation rather than atrial flutter waves, and the wide QRS with extreme axis deviation favors VT.

recommendedActions: Assess for immediate clinical deterioration (BP, mental status)
Prepare for synchronized cardioversion if patient becomes hemodynamically unstable
Obtain 12-lead ECG for formal confirmation and localization
Order serial Troponin T and electrolytes (K, Mg) to optimize myocardial stability
Consult Cardiology for management of VT in the setting of ischemic cardiomyopathy
Continue monitoring; do not withhold Carvedilol unless patient becomes hypotensive
